Definition: a poisonous plant, probably the poppy (from its conspicuous head); generally poison (even of serpents)
BiblicalUsage: Rôʼsh names a poisonous plant, probably the poppy (from its conspicuous head); generally poison (even of serpents). It stands in Amos 6:12, "Shall horses run upon the rock? will plow…", and in Deuteronomy 29:18, "…woman, or family, or tribe, whose heart turneth…".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe rôʼsh is worth knowing, because nothing in Scripture is there by accident.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
